answer: An identity must present an invoice history: invoices issued and paid over years, with the tax authority or the payment provider confirming the record. A sonnet is fourteen lines of discipline, and an invoice history is the same: regular, structured, and sustained. The sable of a farm's invoices is dyed overnight: all issued in one week, all to the same counterparties, all for round numbers. The mirror of a real business reflects varied clients, varied amounts, and years of activity: the network trusts only the reflections that match the provider's own books.
